title: Aamir Khan Begins Major Weight-Loss Transformation to Play a 25-Year-Old in Lalkaara
excerpt: The actor reunites with Lagaan director Ashutosh Gowariker for a sports drama set against the backdrop of Indian cricket and Partition, requiring him to shed significant weight.
body:
• Aamir Khan has begun a major weight-loss program for Lalkaara, a sports drama directed by Ashutosh Gowariker, in which he will portray a 25-year-old character.
  • The film marks the first major Khan-Gowariker collaboration since Lagaan, the 2001 Oscar-nominated cricket epic that turned 25 this year.
  • Lalkaara explores Indian cricket, Partition, and themes of rivalry, friendship, and patriotism, with a script by Piyush Gupta and Neeraj Singh.
  • Farhan Akhtar has exited the project and been replaced by Sidhant Gupta, while Vikrant Massey has been approached for a key role.

A Familiar Collaboration, a New Challenge

Aamir Khan is embarking on another dramatic physical transformation, this time for Lalkaara, a sports drama that reunites him with director Ashutosh Gowariker for the first time since their landmark 2001 film Lagaan. The actor has started a significant weight-loss program to convincingly portray a character roughly half his age, according to an exclusive report by Filmfare.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=1aVw1gZ9Ncg

"Aamir Khan is on a massive weight-loss programme for Ashutosh Gowariker's next film. Touted as a sports drama, Lalkaara will see the actor playing a 25-year-old. Aamir is known to go all out when it comes to physically transforming for a role, and this time too, he is putting in a great deal of work to look convincing."

— Source close to the production, via Filmfare

The reunion has been generating buzz since the project was announced, particularly as it comes in the year Lagaan celebrated its silver jubilee. Khan and Gowariker marked the anniversary in June with a special India Post tribute, and the actor was also photographed reuniting with Lagaan co-star Rachel Shelley in London in July.

The Film's Cricket and Partition Backdrop

Written by Piyush Gupta and Neeraj Singh, Lalkaara is set against the backdrop of Indian cricket and weaves in several dramatic threads — rivalry, friendship, and patriotism among them. The film will also examine the human impact of Partition through the life of one of India's pioneering cricket figures, according to Bollywood Hungama.

https://x.com/filmfare/status/2090769389826293875

The cricket-and-Partition premise carries echoes of Lagaan, which used cricket as a vehicle for a larger narrative about colonial resistance and community. But where Lagaan's Bhuvan was a spirited villager, Khan's character in Lalkaara is described as strikingly different — a role that demands a physical believability that only genuine transformation can provide.

Khan's Track Record of Transformation

Khan, now 61, has built a reputation for pushing his body to match his characters. For Dangal in 2016, he gained 27 kilograms to reach 38 percent body fat before shedding the weight over five months to play the younger version of wrestler Mahavir Singh Phogat. That process involved bringing his body fat down to 9.67 percent through six-to-seven-hour daily training sessions and a strict calorie-controlled diet supervised by U.S.-based dietician Dr. Nikhil Dhurandhar.

For Ghajini in 2008, he trained for 13 months to achieve a muscular physique. For PK in 2014, he adopted an entirely different kind of transformation — softening his mannerisms and voice to portray an alien-like character discovering Earth for the first time. Each project has reinforced the idea that Khan approaches physical preparation as a non-negotiable part of his craft.

A Shifting Cast

The production has seen notable casting developments. Farhan Akhtar, who was initially attached to the project, exited earlier this month, with actor Sidhant Gupta stepping in as his replacement, according to Bollywood Hungama. Separately, Vikrant Massey has been approached for a key role, though no confirmation has followed.

Before Lalkaara took shape, a separate Lala Amarnath biopic had been in development with Shah Rukh Khan and director Rajkumar Hirani, though that project did not materialize. The cricket legend's story ultimately found its way to Gowariker and Khan through a different creative lens.

What to Watch For

No release timeline has been announced for Lalkaara, and with Khan still in the early stages of his physical transformation, production is likely months away from wrapping. For audiences, the project represents a rare double proposition: a Khan comeback vehicle and a Gowariker reunion, both steeped in cricket and history, two subjects that have served Indian cinema well when handled with ambition.
